scenario: [LEXP.3.7.3]: `x.swap_bytes(w)` is the low w/8 bytes of the pattern in reverse order, read through int(). Rule `swapped` fires where `t.x.swap_bytes(t.w)` equals the fact's `want`; every operand is an `Int` slot. `w16`: 0x1234 (4660) at 16 is 0x3412 (13330). `w32`: 0x12345678 (305419896) at 32 is 0x78563412 (2018915346). `w64`: 0x0102030405060708 (72623859790382856) at 64 is 0x0807060504030201 (578437695752307201). `high_dropped`: 0xFF1234 (16716340) at 16 is 0x3412, the bits above the field not reaching the result. `sign`: 0x80 (128) at 64 is INT64_MIN, the byte moving into the sign position. A builtin that kept the high bits would get `high_dropped` wrong, and one that answered only non-negative values would get `sign` wrong. PATH PINNED: FN_SWAP_BYTES in libds (`builtins.c`, `int_ops.h` `ds_i64_swap_bytes`) and Mercury (`ds.eval`).
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    id: String key
    x: Int mutable
    w: Int mutable
    want: Int mutable

rule swapped:
    T t where t.x.swap_bytes(t.w) == t.want
->
    log info "swapped {t.id}"
